'''''Berberis japonica''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Berberidaceae, [[native plant|native]] to [[Taiwan]].<ref name="efloras">[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200008397 Flora of China v 19 p 781, ''Mahonia japonica'']</ref> Despite the name, it is not native to [[Japan]], though it has been known in cultivation there for centuries. The wild origins of this species have long puzzled botanists, but wild plants in Taiwan, previously known under the name ''Mahonia tikushiensis'', appear most similar to the cultivated forms of ''B. japonica''.<ref name="IdentityMjaponica">{{Cite journal |last=Bayton |first=Ross |date=2017 |title=The identity of ''Mahonia japonica'' |journal=The Plantsman |series=New Series |volume=16 |issue=4 |pages=244–248 }}</ref>

==Description==
It is an [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|2|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|3|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} wide.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|page=1136}}</ref> The foliage is [[Pinnation|pinnate]], glossy dark green above, paler beneath, and sharply toothed. Each leaf usually has six to eight pairs of leaflets together with a single terminal [[Leaflet (botany)|leaflet]]. The plant produces new shoots regularly from the base, so it is clothed in foliage at all levels.

The small, scented, yellow flowers are borne from autumn through winter into spring. The [[inflorescence]]s are 25 cm or more long, at first arching and then pendant. Blue or black fruits develop in spring and summer.<ref name="efloras" /><ref>Thunberg, Carl Peter. 1784. Flora Japonica 77, ''Ilex japonica''</ref><ref>Brown, Robert. 1818. Observations systematical and geographical on the herbarium collected by Professor Christian Smith, in the vicinity of the Congo: during the expedition to explore that river, under the command of Captain Tuckey in the year 1816. London, App. 22, ''Berberis japonica''</ref><ref>Candolle, Augustin Pyramus de. 1821.  Regni Vegetabilis Systema Naturale 2: 22.</ref><ref>Hayata, Bunzô. 1915. Icones plantarum formosanarum nec non et contributiones ad floram formosanam 5: 5–6, ''Mahonia tikushiensis''</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Berberis japonica'' was initially scientifically described and named by [[Carl Peter Thunberg]] as ''Ilex japonica'' in 1784, believing it to be a true [[holly]].<ref name="POWO">{{cite POWO |id=106792-1 |title=''Berberis japonica'' (Thunb.) Spreng. |access-date=12 November 2023}}</ref> In 1821 [[Augustin Pyramus de Candolle]] reclassified it as ''Mahonia japonica''. Disagreeing with this, [[Kurt Polycarp Joachim Sprengel]] classified it in ''[[Berberis]]'' as ''Berberis japonica'' in 1825.<ref name="POWO" /> A paper was published by [[Joseph Edward Laferrière]] in 1997 summarized the arguments for ''[[Mahonia]]'' being more properly classified as a [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] of ''Berberis''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Laferrière |first1=Joseph Edward |title=Transfer of Specific and Infraspecific Taxa from ''Mahonia'' to ''Berberis'' (Berberidaceae) |journal=Botanicheskii Zhurnal |date=1997 |volume=82 |issue=9 |pages=95–97 |url=http://en.arch.botjournal.ru/?t=issues&id=19970909&rid=pdf_0005055 |access-date=8 November 2023 |archive-date=7 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231107012402/http://en.arch.botjournal.ru/?t=issues&id=19970909&rid=pdf_0005055 |url-status=dead }}</ref> As of 2023 this is the most common classification by botanists.<ref name="POWO" />

==Cultivation==
The plant is much grown as an ornamental shrub, and for use in landscapes. It is of value for its bold foliage, flowers in flowering season, and as a [[groundcover]] landscape shrub. Its spiny foliage invite use in security hedging.

''Berberis japonica'' has received the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web 
| url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/10734/i-Mahonia-japonica-i/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Mahonia japonica''
| access-date = 25 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 62 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 25 March 2018}}</ref>  The [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrid]] between it and [[Berberis oiwakensis|''Berberis oiwakensis'' subsp. ''lomariifolia'']] is also a popular garden plant. Known as [[Berberis × hortensis|''Berberis'' × ''hortensis'']], several [[cultivar]]s have been developed from it, including 'Charity', 'Winter Sun' and 'Lionel Fortescue'.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Brickell |first=C.D. |date=1979 |title=The hybrids between ''Berberis japonica'' and ''M. lomariifolia'' |journal=The Plantsman |volume=1 |pages=12–20}}</ref> A hybrid with [[Berberis napaulensis|''Berberis napaulensis'' var. ''napaulensis'']] (''M. siamensis''), called ''Mahonia'' × ''lindsayae'' 'Cantab', though less well known, is a useful garden plant<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cullen |first=J. |date=2012 |title=''Mahonia'' × ''lindsayae'' 'Cantab' |journal=Curtis's Botanical Magazine| volume=29|issue=2 |pages=122–136|doi=10.1111/j.1467-8748.2012.01778.x }}</ref> and also holds an Award of Garden Merit.<ref name="RHSAZ" />

''[[Berberis bealei]],'' native to [[mainland China]]<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200008385 Flora of China v 19 p 778, ''Mahonia bealei'']</ref> and also widely cultivated, is usually treated as a separate species, but in the past has been listed as a cultivar of ''Berberis japonica''.<ref name="IdentityMjaponica" /> Its most obvious differences from ''B. japonica'' are in shorter, upright flowering [[raceme]]s and wider leaflets.
